jobs.occupation: Fullstack Developer – Join Us in Building the Platform of the Future
jobs.description:

We are looking for an experienced Full-Stack Developer who wants to do more than just write code. You will have a significant influence on technology choices, architecture, and product development, while remaining hands-on with the codebase every day.

What You’ll Do

• 
Take technical ownership of the continued development of the platform.

• 
Design and implement scalable architecture to support the next phase of growth.

• 
Develop frontend and backend solutions in close collaboration with the team.

• 
Drive high standards of quality through effective development processes, testing, and code reviews.

• 
Explore and implement AI-powered solutions that deliver greater value to our customers and business.

• 
Work closely with product, business, and commercial teams to translate needs into effective solutions.

What We’re Looking For

• 
Experience as a Full-Stack Developer, ideally with experience in a technical leadership or coordinating role.

• 
Strong skills in HTML, CSS, C#, .NET, EF Core, and unit testing.

• 
Experience with React/TypeScript for component-based and modular development.

• 
A solid understanding of SQL databases (MS SQL Server) and continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD).

• 
Hands-on experience using AI tools in software development. You are AI-savvy and actively leverage AI to improve both speed and quality.

• 
Experience in a startup or scale-up environment, or the ability to thrive in a fast-moving, dynamic setting.

• 
A customer-focused and proactive mindset, with strong written and verbal communication skills in English. Fluency in Norwegian is a plus.

• 
A structured yet creative approach, with the confidence to challenge conventional thinking.

What We Offer

• 
A chance to join an exciting journey with global potential.

• 
An inclusive and inspiring culture driven by ambition, collaboration, and respect.

• 
Competitive salary and benefits, including stock options to foster ownership.

• 
Close collaboration with experienced investors and entrepreneurs.

• 
A dynamic workplace where your contributions make a real impact.

About Availy

Availy is a disruptive technology company on an exciting journey. We are building a growth platform that automates resource management and booking, professionalizes operations, and makes it easier for businesses to grow.

Our three core values define how we operate

• 
Ambition: Dare to take risks and learn from honest mistakes, making us bolder for the future.

• 
Dignity: Stay true to yourself and trust your colleagues to make the right choices in any situation.

• 
Unity: Collaborate for the greater good across our employees, customers, and stakeholders.

jobs.occupation: Head of Sales (Nordics)
jobs.description:
About Us
At No Isolation, we’re a profitable, 65-person Norwegian EdTech scale-up operating across Europe. We help educators bring learning and belonging to every child.

Our AV1 robot is deployed in 19 countries, with 5,000+ units supporting schools to improve attendance, belonging, and continuity of learning for children who cannot be physically present. Consistently described as life-changing, it bridges the gap between the student and their peers, restoring both educational continuity and the essential sense of social belonging.

We’re established enough to have a proven solution and strong financial foundations, yet still small enough for every new colleague to have a visible impact on our next stage of growth.

The Opportunity - Head of Sales, Nordics
You’ve led sales teams selling to kommuner and other public sector clients. You know how to multi-thread across multiple stakeholders, navigate decision and budget processes, and like being hands-on the most important of deals. Now you want a new challenge with a strong team to develop, and a solution customers actually need and want.

The Nordics are our home market - with some of our best market penetration, where customers rarely churn, yet with lots of market opportunity still to capture. We’re looking for someone who will lead from the front and help a small team across Norway, Sweden and Denmark drive our growth.

What your week looks like
• 
Joining your Account Managers in their customer meetings and helping them close.

• 
Deal reviews and pipeline check-ins with the team.

• 
Working with Marketing, Product and Customer Success on what’s coming next.

• 
Attending and speaking at industry events where our customers are.

What you’ll own
• 
Your own portfolio of key municipal and education accounts, from first meeting to signed agreement.

• 
The move from single-school sales to framework agreements with kommuner and education authorities.

• 
The team’s results across three markets that each need their own plan.

• 
Where we focus: which segments, territories and accounts are worth the push.

• 
A pipeline and forecast in HubSpot that you’re happy to stand behind.

You are probably someone who
• 
Has a track record leading B2B/B2G sales teams - ideally has sold to Norwegian kommuner or other public sector clients, and knows how budgets, politics and procurement work. Experience from other Nordic countries or the Baltics is a plus.

• 
Until recently carried a quota, and/or has remained heavily involved in shaping and closing deals yourself.

• 
Has led and coached account managers, and knows that different people need different support to improve and perform their best.

• 
Understands the importance of sales methodologies, whether that’s MEDDPICC, SPIN, Challenger or similar.

• 
Is data driven and uses CRM (HubSPot a plus) to understand trends and drive performance.

• 
Speaks fluent Norwegian and English. Swedish or Danish is a bonus.

• 
Is based in Oslo and happy with a hybrid setup.

Who you’ll work with
You’ll report to our CCO, Sanjeev, who is based in London and previously led Vodafone business units across Africa and Europe. From our Oslo HQ you’ll work closely with our CEO, Morten, a former McKinsey Partner, and an experienced Leadership Team.

What’s in it for you
• 
Real earning potential. We offer uncapped commission beyond OTE. The need is high and the solution proven - it now requires someone to drive systematic execution.

• 
A solution that sells. It’s unique, backed by evidence of impact and significantly more cost-effective compared to alternatives. Our churn is very low - the solution works and customers love it.

• 
Something to build on. You’re taking over a successful team that now needs taking up to the next level.

• 
A place people like working. Our engagement scores are above benchmark, and we have structured onboarding with a buddy, an annual company trip and great collaboration across teams.

• 
Enhanced parental and sick leave.

• 
Flexible hours around a 10:00–15:00 core, with the option to work remotely.

• 
Central office in Oslo.

• 
27 vacation days.

• 
Travel insurance for you and your immediate family.

• 
Mobile phone and internet subscription.

Location
This role is based in our Oslo HQ office, with regular travel across Norway, Sweden and Denmark to support your team in the field.

We believe in-person leadership matters, so we work a flexible hybrid model built around real collaboration.

How to Apply
Please click Apply and upload your CV in English.

If you’d like, you can also include a short video (in English) as part of your application – this is optional, but it gives us a chance to see a bit more of who you are beyond your CV. Let your personality and passion shine!

If you're looking for a leadership role where the demand is already proven and the job is to build on that - not create it from scratch - we'd love to hear from you.

🎥 You can watch how AV1 transforms inclusion in education here: vimeo.com/1098745115

🌍 You can explore our mission and impact stories at noisolation.com

We kindly ask external recruitment agencies and consultants to refrain from contacting us regarding this position.

Om arbeidsgiveren:
We help educators bring learning and belonging to every child.

School absence is the biggest challenge facing education. Our AV1 robots connect absent students, ensure learning and belonging, and support reintegration back to the classroom.

Today, there are over 3,500 active AV1 robots used across 18 European countries. Positioned in the EdTech sector, AV1 is a unique solution to the growing issue of persistent absence, supporting both the academic and social needs of students.

No Isolation works across Europe, with 45 employees across Europe and in offices in Oslo, Munich and London. Join us in our growth journey!

jobs.occupation: St. nr. 11/2026 - PhD Position in Mathematics Education, Artificial Intelligence and Competence Dev
jobs.employer_name: HØGSKULEN I VOLDA AVD FOR HUMANISTISKE FAG OG LÆRERUT
jobs.description:
The position
Faculty of Humanities and education, The Department of Science and Mathematics at Volda University College invites applications for a three-year PhD Position in mathematics education, artificial intelligence (AI) and competence development.

The position is linked to research activities within TRUST (The Norwegian Centre for Trustworthy AI), one of Norway’s national research centres for artificial intelligence. 

The successful candidate will apply for admission to the PhD programme in Education, Language and Culture at Volda University College. The programme takes an interdisciplinary approach, incorporating perspectives on teaching and learning across different subject areas.

The PhD project will be developed in close collaboration with the supervisors within the research framework outlined in this announcement. The candidate is expected to start as soon as possible after appointment.
The research project
Artificial intelligence is transforming education, working life and society, creating a need for new knowledge about the competencies people require in an AI-rich society. The project focuses particularly on mathematical competencies relevant to the development, use and understanding of AI, including modelling, abstraction, statistical reasoning and algorithmic thinking.

The candidate will develop an independent doctoral research project within this broad framework. Possible areas of investigation may include:

• which mathematical and AI-related competencies will become important in a society shaped by AI
• how such competencies are integrated into education and can be developed through educational practice
• how teaching approaches, learning resources and initiatives for competence development can be designed
• how such initiatives can be investigated and evaluated in authentic educational settings
• how AI may shape students’ opportunities for mathematics learning, academic support and developing life skills across home, school and everyday settings
• how these changes may help reduce social and educational inequalities and support participation and democratic development
The project will be rooted in mathematics education research. The final research questions, theoretical framework and research design will be developed in collaboration with the supervisors.

Through TRUST – The Norwegian Centre for Trustworthy AI, and its more than 70 national and international partners from academia, industry, government, and civil society, the candidate will have access to an extensive national and international research network.

TRUST is advancing trustworthy AI that is accurate, interpretable, inclusive, fair, safe, sustainable and well governed. Combining expertise in (i) machine learning, statistics, mathematics, and data science, (ii) law, and social sciences, and (iii) philosophy, the centre develops AI technologies and interdisciplinary frameworks, supports innovation and examines AI’s impact on democracy, the rule of law, and the environment. Research spans theoretical, methodological, legal and empirical perspectives, tested in real-world contexts, including healthcare, mobility, governance, security, and climate resilience. Users, citizens and civil society organisations contribute to assessing the trustworthiness of research and innovation. 

TRUST is funded by the Research Council of Norway and public and private partners, and is led by the University of Oslo, SINTEF and the Norwegian Computing Center (NR). 
Responsibilities
The candidate will:

• carry out an independent doctoral research project
• plan and conduct research activities and data collection
• analyse research data and publish findings
• disseminate research through academic publications, conferences and other relevant forums
• participate actively in the research community at Volda University College and in TRUST-related activities
• collaborate with national and international research partners and practitionersRequired qualifications
Applicants must have:

• a master’s degree or equivalent qualification in mathematics education, mathematics, computing education, educational sciences or a closely related field
• an academic background qualifying for admission to the PhD programme in Education, Language and Culture at Volda University College, normally with grades equivalent to B or higher
• good spoken and written English skills
Desirable qualifications

We particularly welcome applicants who can demonstrate one or more of the following:

• documented competence in mathematics teaching or mathematics education, for example through teaching, research, development work or teacher education
• documented knowledge of or experience with AI, digital technology, programming, data analysis or related areas
• competence in mathematical modelling, statistics or statistical analysis
• experience with qualitative and/or quantitative research methods
• research experience in mathematics education, educational sciences or a related field
• familiarity with the Norwegian or another Scandinavian education system, curriculum development or competence development
Proficiency in Norwegian or another Scandinavian language is an advantage, particularly for collaboration with schools, data collection and research dissemination, but is not a requirement.

Personal qualities

We are seeking a candidate who:

• is intellectually curious and motivated to undertake doctoral research
• works independently and systematically
• has strong collaboration and communication skills
• is motivated and committed to contribute actively to an interdisciplinary research environment
Personal suitability will be taken into account.
We offer
• a fully funded three-year PhD position
• an active community of doctoral candidates affiliated with the PhD programme in Education, Language and Culture
• a strong research environment in science, mathematics, and mathematics education at Volda University College
• participation in research activities and networks associated with TRUST
• excellent opportunities for national and international research collaboration
• salary in accordance with the Norwegian state salary scale and membership of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK). The starting salary is set at NOK 580,000, with an automatic annual progression of 3% for a maximum of 4 years.General information
Volda University College is committed to diversity and encourages qualified applicants to apply regardless of age, gender, disability, or ethnic background.

The appointment will be made in accordance with the terms and conditions applicable to the position. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interview.

Applications must be submitted electronically via Jobbnorge. A public list of applicants will be drawn up after the application deadline. Applicants who wish to request exemption from the public list must provide reasons for this in their application.
 Application requirements
Applications must include:

• a cover letter and a statement of motivation (1–2 pages) explaining the applicant’s motivation and how their academic background and expertise are relevant to the position
• a curriculum vitae (CV)
• degree certificates and academic transcripts
• a writing sample, such as a master’s thesis, manuscript or published article
• the names and contact details of 2–3 referees 
The PhD project will be developed in collaboration with the supervisors after appointment.

Applications may be written in English, Norwegian, or another Scandinavian language.
Contact
For further information about the position, please contact:

• Arve Fiskerstrand, Associate Professor, Department of Science and Mathematics, arve.fiskerstrand@hivolda.no
• Andreas Brandsæter, Professor, Department of Science and Mathematics, andreas.brandsaeter@hivolda.noStudiebygda Volda
Midt mellom fjord og fjell på spektakulære Sunnmøre finn du Høgskulen i Volda, med sine lange tradisjonar.

Les meir på www.hivolda.no
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wSlL1WkuUXc
Om arbeidsgiveren:

Høgskulen i Volda er høgskulen for humaniora og samfunnsvitskap i Møre og Romsdal. Vi er ein spennande kompetanseorganisasjon i vekst med om lag 4500 studentar og 380 tilsette. Vi gjev undervisning i ei rekkje fagområde, yrkesretta utdanningar og etter- og vidareutdanningar i nært samarbeid med samfunns- og næringsliv. Høgskulen i Volda driv mykje forsking og utviklingsarbeid og satsar på forskaropplæring og kompetanseoppbygging for dei tilsette i samarbeid med universitet i inn- og utland.

jobs.occupation: PhD Research Fellow position in Knowledge-Grounded LLM Agents for Defensive Cyber Operations
jobs.description:
About the position
We invite applications for a PhD Research Fellow position in Knowledge-Grounded LLM Agents for Defensive Cyber Operations, available at the Digital Security Research Group within the Department of Informatics at the University of Oslo.

Starting date as soon as possible and no later than 01.05.2027. The fellowship period is three years.

A fourth year may be considered, which would involve 25% other career-promoting work. Other career-promoting work may consist of teaching, supervision, and/or research assistance. This depends on the applicant's qualifications and the department's current needs.

No one can be appointed for more than one PhD Research Fellowship period at the University of Oslo.
Project description
The position will investigate knowledge-grounded and neuro-symbolic approaches to large language models and agentic AI for defensive cyber operations. The PhD project will be carried out in close collaboration with the Norwegian Defence Research Establishment (FFI), including co-supervision from FFI with potential to connect the research to relevant cybersecurity and cyber-defence challenges.

The research will explore how heterogeneous cybersecurity intelligence and evidence sources, including telemetry and observations, can be transformed into structured cybersecurity knowledge, represented through semantic knowledge graphs, and combined with symbolic reasoning, modern language models, and autonomous agents to support security analysis, situational awareness, decision-making, and response. Particular emphasis will be placed on developing trustworthy, reliable, interpretable, and secure AI systems, including methods for grounding, reasoning, validation, and the control of agentic behaviour in security-critical environments. 
 
The security and robustness of LLM-based and agentic systems, including adversarial manipulation, uncertainty, provenance, and the validation of AI-generated decisions and actions, may also be explored as part of this position.
What skills are important in this role?
The Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences has a strategic ambition to be among Europe’s leading communities for research, education and innovation. Candidates for these fellowships will be selected in accordance with this, and expected to be in the upper segment of their class with respect to academic credentials.

Required qualifications:

• Master’s degree or equivalent in cybersecurity, computer science (informatics), artificial intelligence, or a closely related field. Foreign completed degree (M.Sc.-level) corresponding to a minimum of four years in the Norwegian educational system
• Strong foundation in computer science or artificial intelligence/machine learning, with knowledge of cybersecurity or a demonstrated motivation to apply AI/ML in cybersecurity
• Strong programming and software development skills, demonstrated through relevant projects, research, or equivalent experience
• Fluent oral and written communication skills in English
Candidates who have not yet completed their master’s degree must have completed all requirements for the degree by 31.12.2026.

The position will involve cooperation with stakeholders related to Norwegian national security, and candidates' suitability for this will also be taken into account.

Desired qualifications:

• Knowledge of or experience with large language models (LLMs), agentic AI, and related AI/ML methods
• Knowledge of or experience with semantic technologies, including knowledge graphs, ontologies, knowledge representation, and/or symbolic reasoning
• Knowledge of or experience with cybersecurity, particularly cybersecurity operations, security analysis, threat detection and response, cyber threat intelligence, or security automation
• Knowledge of or interest in trustworthy and secure AI, including robustness, interpretability, validation, uncertainty, or the security of LLM-based and agentic systems
• Previous research experience, for example, through a master’s thesis, scientific publication, research project, or equivalent work, is considered an advantage
Language requirement:

• Good oral and written communication skills in English
• English requirements for applicants from outside of EU/ EEA countries and exemptions from the requirements:https://www.mn.uio.no/english/research/phd/regulations/regulations.html#toc8
Grade requirements:The norm is as follows:

• The average grade point for courses included in the Bachelor’s degree must be C or better in the Norwegian educational system
• The average grade point for courses included in the Master’s degree must be B or better in the Norwegian educational system
• The Master’s thesis must have the grade B or better in the Norwegian educational system
For more information see:

The purpose of the fellowship is research training leading to the successful completion of a PhD degree. 

UiO is subject to the Security Act, which governs the organisation's protection of security-sensitive objects and knowledge, in addition to other relevant legislation concerning access to and handling of sensitive information. Based on this, it is a requirement that successful applicants are security-eligible. We may use background checks as part of our recruitment process.
What are we looking for in you?
Personal skills:

• Ability to work independently and take initiative, while also contributing effectively to collaborative research
• Analytical, critical, and structured approach to research and problem-solving
• Curiosity and willingness to learn, with the ability to adapt to new research questions, methods, and technologies
• Good communication and collaboration skills, and the ability to engage constructively in interdisciplinary research
• Positive attitude and the ability to handle hectic periods
Employment in the position is based on a comprehensive assessment of all qualification requirements applicable to the position, including personal qualifications.
We can offer you
• Exciting and meaningful tasks in an organisation with an important societal mission, contributing to knowledge development, education, and enlightenment that promote sustainable, fair, and knowledge-based societal development
• Committed colleagues in a good working environment
• Good welfare schemes
• Opportunity of up to 1.5 hours a week of exercise during working hours
• A workplace with good development and career opportunities
• Career development programmes
• Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemes
• Oslo’s family-friendly surroundings with their rich opportunities for culture and outdoor activities
• Salary in position as PhD Research Fellow, position code 1017 in salary range NOK from 550 800 - 595 000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, 2 percent is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund We need different perspectives in our work
UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues, could you be the next one?

We will do our best to accommodate your needs. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.

If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps (Norwegian), we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports. More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here. We hope you will apply for the position with us.
How to apply
The application must include:

• Cover letter (statement of motivation, summarising scientific work and research interest)
• CV (summarising education, positions, pedagogical experience, administrative experience and other qualifying activity)
• Transcripts of records, copies of the original Bachelor’s and Master’s degree diplomas (see below)
• Documentation of English Language requirements. The appointed candidate cannot start in the position until approved documentation of English language proficiency has been submitted.
• A complete list of publications and related academic or research works, including software artefacts that the applicant wishes to be considered by the evaluation committee
• Names and contact details of 2-3 references (name, relation to candidate, e-mail and telephone number)
Application with attachments must be submitted via our recruitment system Jobbnorge, click "Apply for this job".Foreign applicants should attach an official explanation of their University's grading system.

When applying for the position, we ask you to retrieve your education results from Vitnemålsportalen.no. If your education results are not available through Vitnemålsportalen, we ask you to upload copies of your transcripts or grades. Please note that all documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language.
General information
The best qualified candidates will be invited for interviews.Applicant lists can be published in accordance with Norwegian Freedom of Information Act § 25. When you apply for a position with us, your name will appear on the public applicant list. It is possible to request to be excluded from this list. You must justify why you want an exemption from publication and we will then decide whether we can grant your request. If we can't, you will hear from us.
 
Please refer to Regulations for the Act on universities and colleges chapter 3 (Norwegian), Guidelines concerning appointment to post doctoral and research posts at UiO (Norwegian) and Regulations for the degree of Philosophiae Doctor (PhD) at the University of Oslo.  

The University of Oslo has a transfer agreement with all employees that is intended to secure the rights to all research results etc.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and highest rated institution of research and education with 26 500 students and 7 200 employees. Its broad range of academic disciplines and internationally esteemed research communities make UiO an important contributor to society. 

The Department of Informatics (IFI) is one of nine departments belonging to the Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences. IFI is Norway’s largest university department for general education and research in Computer Science and related topics. 

The Department has more than 1800 students on bachelor level, 600 master students, and over 240 PhDs and postdocs. The overall staff of the Department is close to 370 employees, about 280 of these in full time positions. The full time tenured academic staff is 75, mostly Full/Associate Professors.

jobs.occupation: Hardware Reliability Manager
jobs.description:
Nofence is a Norwegian scale-up that has built the world’s first virtual fencing solution for livestock. As we aim to revolutionize livestock management, we need top-notch competence in our Engineering team, and we are now looking for an Hardware Reliability Manager for our Hardware Reliability Team.

Hardware Reliability Team
Our Hardware Reliability Team works with quality at both ends of our product life cycle. First: Validation of new livestock product designs, and second: monitoring and identifying failures on products in the field. These tasks are split into two disciplines: validation and failure analysis. As Hardware Reliability Manager, you will lead both of these teams. You will have a holistic view of the real-life conditions of our products, and ensure that these conditions are replicated in the lab. What can not be replicated in the lab has to be validated in the field on test farms around the globe. You will also monitor product performance, coordinate field investigations, and recommend mitigations of quality issues together with other stakeholders.

Your main responsibilities will be:
• 
Shape the overall validation and quality strategy to match business goals and risk tolerance.

• 
Lead the Hardware Reliability Team across new and existing products - setting priorities, allocating resources across projects, clearing roadblocks, and keeping the team on track.

• 
Deliver clear, structured reporting on test progress, pass/fail metrics, and overall quality status.

• 
Own end-to-end mechanical, electronics, and embedded validation plans from early product development through mass production and failure analysis.

• 
Serve as a service point for internal stakeholders on validation and product quality.

• 
Plan, conduct, and execute field testing under real-world operating conditions to validate product performance and catch issue trends early.

• 
Monitor collar performance in the field after we release the product.

• 
Coordinate validation activities delivered to the engineering and manufacturing teams.

We are looking for someone who has:
• 
Bachelor or Master degree in engineering or another relevant degree

• 
Experience with leading engineering activities within hardware and software

• 
Experience with leading cross-functional teams at a technical level

• 
Excellent analytical skills

• 
Proven project management skills

• 
Knowledge of international testing standards

We are looking for someone who is:
• 
Motivated by working in an autonomous cross-functional team.

• 
Thrives in a fast-paced development environment and can rapidly assess and prioritize critical issues.

• 
Structured with the ability to bridge the gap between engineers and internal and external stakeholders.

• 
Willing and able to travel across the Nordic region and internationally to meet with end-users and colleagues.

• 
Comfortable working in an English-speaking environment.

About Nofence
Managing livestock has always been a challenge. Humanity has tried everything from herding with dogs to walling the animals in with barbed wire, electric, and wooden fences, but these are costly and time-consuming solutions and often in conflict with the local wildlife. It has also left vast areas of potential pasture overgrown and underutilized.

Until now.

Enter virtual fences. What started as a small group of farmers and engineers with a big idea has become Nofence – the world’s first virtual fencing solution for livestock.

What we bring to the table
At Nofence, we're not your typical 9-to-5 gig. We're a dynamic scale-up, creating a work atmosphere that's anything but ordinary. It's a place where dedication and innovation are the norm, offering great opportunities for your personal and professional growth.

We believe in seeing results fast. As a manager, your work won't be lost in the bureaucratic shuffle. You'll witness the immediate impact of your contributions in real-time, influencing the evolution of our cutting-edge virtual fencing solution for livestock.

Join us, where ambition meets reality, and let's keep pushing the boundaries in the world of agri-tech!

About the Application
Please submit your application directly through this portal. In line with applicable data protection regulations and our data protection practices, we are unable to accept or process applications received by email. Applying through the portal also ensures your personal data is handled securely. We will evaluate candidates continuously and look forward to hearing from you! If you have any questions about Nofence or the application, please reach out to our VP Engineering Fabien Lepoutre at below email.

Målsettingen til Nofence er å få beitedyra ut på beite, på en trygg og god måte, slik at de kan ha det godt og selv finne den maten de er skapt for å spise.Vi vil at beitedyr skal få muligheten til å ta i bruk sitt naturlige miljø. Det er god dyrevelferd og det vil frigjøre store arealer som kan brukes til å dyrke menneskemat i stedet for soya i kraftforproduksjon.Vår teknologi gir dyra denne muligheten.

jobs.description:

Hva vi ser etter
Qualifications

• 

Valid Category B driving licence -- required

• 

Comfortable driving regularly as part of the working day

• 

Able to perform practical and physical work

• 

Able to communicate in English or Norwegian

• 

Previous experience from logistics, warehouse work, property services or similar work is an advantage, but not required

Personal qualities

We are looking for someone who:

• 

Is reliable and responsible

• 

Works independently and efficiently

• 

Is organised and keeps good overview

• 

Is flexible and comfortable with changing daily tasks

• 

Is practical and solution-oriented

• 

Takes responsibility for completing assigned tasks

• 

Is comfortable working outdoors in winter conditions

A large part of the working day will involve driving our company vehicle between our warehouse, laundry provider and rental properties.

Receive clean bed linen from the laundry provider

• 

Sort and organise linen at the warehouse

• 

Prepare linen for distribution to our properties

• 

Deliver clean linen to rental properties

• 

Collect used linen from properties

Sort and prepare used linen for return

Deliver or return used linen to the laundry provider or agreed collection point

Maintain good order and overview at the warehouse

Use and take care of the company vehicle during daily logistics operations

Keep entrances, stairs and access areas accessible and safe for guests

A practical and independent role in a growing short-term rental company

Company vehicle available for work-related driving

Varied working days across our property portfolio in Tromsø

Training and clear routines for the role

A flexible and informal working environment

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Fellows in Educational Measurement
jobs.description:
Job description
Applications are invited for 1-2 full time positions for three- to four-years as Postdoctoral Fellows at the Centre for Research on Equality in Education (CREATE), Faculty of Educational Sciences, University of Oslo, Norway. The positions have a double affiliation with the Centre for Educational Measurement (CEMO).

CREATE is an interdisciplinary Centre of Excellence funded by the Research Council of Norway with the objective to generate novel knowledge about how to reduce inequalities in education. The interdisciplinary center integrates researchers with substantive expertise from education, psychology, sociology, economics, and genetics, and methodological expertise from educational measurement, psychometrics, econometrics, statistics, and biostatistics. The Postdoctoral Fellowships are affiliated with CREATE’s research strand 3 «Addressing key methodological challenges».  

CEMO provides a stimulating research environment by bringing internationally renowned substantive and methodological experts together. Research at CEMO combines basic research and applications of advanced measurement techniques to solve core educational problems. CEMO also contributes to the development of measurement competence through teaching and outreach.
More about the positions
The positions are tied to strand 3 of CREATE, which aims to develop novel methods and statistical software that are tailor-made to the research questions and data of CREATE. 

The successful candidate will conduct advanced methodological and psychometric research. Potential research areas include (a) instructional sensitivity and opportunity to learn in international large-scale assessments in education, (b) estimation and inference methods for weighted generalized structural equation models with mixed continuous and discrete data in longitudinal settings, and (c) advancing research synthesis and meta-analytic methods, for instance, to investigate digital inequalities in education using international large-scale assessment data.

The appointments are full-time positions and made for a period of three years, 10% of which is devoted to required duties, usually in the form of teaching activities. If there is a good match between the candidate’s competence and the teaching needs at CEMO, the positions may be extended to four years, 25% of which is devoted to required duties, usually in the form of teaching activities and supervision. For these positions, the teaching activities will be part of CEMO’s master’s programme in Assessment, Measurement and Evaluation.

The main purpose of the fellowship is to build a research profile and competence that qualifies the postdoctoral fellow to apply for a position as associate professor within their disciplines. The position may also provide other competence with relevance for the postdoctoral fellow's further career.

If the Postdoctoral Fellow does not already have educational qualifications that meet the requirements for an associate professor position, UiO shall facilitate the acquisition of such competence during the employment period.

A career plan shall be developed for the Postdoctoral Fellow, specifying the competencies the Postdoctoral Fellow should acquire. UiO is responsible for following up on the career plan and ensuring that the Postdoctoral Fellow has access to career guidance throughout the postdoctoral term.
Qualification requirements
• Applicants must hold a degree equivalent to a Norwegian doctoral degree in one of the social and behavioral sciences, statistics, or computer science applying and/or developing advanced quantitative methods. The doctoral dissertation must have been submitted for evaluation by the application deadline. Appointment is dependent on the public defense of the doctoral thesis being approved
• Fluent oral and written communication skills in English 
• Demonstrated fit to one of the three research areas (a) to (c) listed above
• Proficiency in programming and data analysis in the statistical software environment R, Python, or other relevant programming languages, as evidenced in relevant courses or publication(s)
Applicants will be evaluated as a function of the fit between their qualifications and the research area they apply for. The following qualifications will count in the assessment of the applicants:

• For research area (a), prior experience with IRT/mixed-effects logistic regression and international large-scale assessments in education
• For research area (b), prior experience with latent variable models and Monte Carlo simulation studies
• For research area (c), prior experience with meta-analysis/research synthesis and international large-scale assessment dataPersonal skills
• Creativity and ability to work independently 
• Self-motivated, eager to learn and ready to tackle and deal with challenges
• Able to collaborate with others 
Personal suitability and motivation for the position will be emphasized.
We need different perspectives in our work
UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues—could you be the next one?

We will do our best to accommodate your needs. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.
 
If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps (Norwegian), we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports. More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here. 

We hope you will apply for the position with us.
We offer
• Salary NOK 595 000 - 670 000 per annum depending on qualifications in position as Postdoctoral Research Fellow (position code 1352). From the salary, 2 percent is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund
• A professionally stimulating work environment
• An interdisciplinary and international work environment, recognized as a Centre of Excellence
• Attractive welfare benefits 
• Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemesHow to apply
The application must include:

• Cover letter (maximum two pages), including a statement of motivation and your fit with one of the research areas (a) to (c) listed above 
• CV (summarizing education, positions, pedagogical experience, administrative experience and other qualifying activity)
• Copy of PhD Diploma or documentation of thesis submission. Applicants who have not yet defended their PhD dissertation need to include an advisor's letter confirming specific expectations about when the degree will be received
• Copy of the PhD thesis 
• Copies of educational certificates (academic transcripts only)
• A complete list of publications
• List of reference persons: 2-3 references (name, relation to candidate, e-mail and phone number)
The application with attachments must be delivered in our electronic recruiting system Jobbnorge. Foreign applicants are advised to attach an explanation of their University's grading system. Please note that all documents should be in English (or a Scandinavian language).

Incomplete applications will not be assessed. 

In assessing the applicants, special emphasis will be placed on the documented, academic qualifications, as well as the candidates motivation and personal suitability. Interviews with the best qualified candidates will be arranged.

It is expected that the successful candidate will be able to complete the project in the course of the period of employment.
Formal regulations
Please refer to Regulations for the Act on universities and colleges chapter 3 (Norwegian) and the guidelines and regulations for appointments to Postdoctoral Fellowships at the University of Oslo.

No one can be appointed for more than one Postdoctoral Fellow period at the University of Oslo.

Applicant lists can be published in accordance with the Norwegian Freedom and Information Act § 25. When you apply for a position, your name will appear on the public applicant list. It is possible to request to be excluded from this list. You must justify why you want an exemption from publication and we will then decide whether we can grant your request. If we cannot, you will hear from us.

The University of Oslo has an agreement for all employees, aiming to secure rights to research results etc.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and highest ranked educational and research institution, with 27 400 students and 6 900 employees. With its broad range of academic disciplines and internationally recognised research communities, UiO is an important contributor to society.

CREATE (Centre of Research on Equality in Education) is an interdisciplinary Centre of Excellence funded by the Research Council of Norway and the Faculty of Educational Sciences. CREATE’s objective is to generate novel knowledge about how to reduce inequalities in education.
